title: Cold rebuild: find and stop real processes
summary: List PIDs with pgrep and stop processes with the right signal, from memory.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a skill stuck. In *Processes and signals* you found real processes and stopped them with the right
signal. Now do it again from memory: the same scenario, **no hints, no solution to peek at**. The checks are
exactly the ones you passed the first time.
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old commands feels like knowing
them; typing them cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: The server is slow. Which command shows you, **live**, which process is eating the CPU?
steps.explain: `ps` is a snapshot; `top`/`htop` refresh continuously. `df -h` is disk space.

steps.title: Find and stop real processes, cold
prompt: Five programs run in the background again.
1. `~/answers/pids.txt`: the PIDs of all `report-worker` processes, one per line.
2. Stop `stuck-export` so that it can save its progress to `~/export.log`.
3. Make sure `noisy-logger`, which ignores the polite signal, is gone. Leave the workers running.
From memory: no hints this time.
